A rare genetic mutation called pseudo-melanism has resulted in roughly half of the tigers in India's Similipal Tiger Reserve sporting coats with far more black than those of usual tigers. This widespread coloration is a symptom of a shallow gene pool in a region that previously faced a dwindling tiger population, and could prove catastrophic if conservation officers aren't able to find these tigers more genetically diverse mates. ♯ FW !!! TIGER CANINES👀👀 ♯ Tigers possess 30 highly specialized teeth designed exclusively for a predatory lifestyle. Their upper jaw holds 16 teeth, while the lower jaw contains 14, only moving vertically without any side-to-side grinding. Dominating their mouth are the canine teeth, which grow between 2.5 and 4 inches (6.4 to 10 cm) long, making them the largest of any living cat species. These massive fangs are embedded with pressure-sensitive nerves that allow the tiger to feel exactly where to place a lethal bite to sever a victim's spinal cord or windpipe. A wide gap called a diastema separates these front weapons from the sharp, scissor-like carnassial teeth at the back, which shear meat into swallowable chunks without chewing. While born completely toothless, tigers quickly develop temporary milk teeth before their permanent adult set grows in to deliver an incredible bite force of up to 1,100 PSI ⌣  #tiger #canines #teeth #pantheriatigris #fyp

The tiger (Panthera tigris) is the largest living cat species, recognised by its powerful body, sharp claws, muscular limbs, and distinctive orange coat covered in black stripes. Tigers are skilled hunters with exceptional night vision, strong jaws, and the ability to move quietly through dense vegetation. Unlike most cats, they are also excellent swimmers and often use rivers and lakes to cool down or travel. Tigers symbolise strength, courage, independence, and raw power. They inhabit forests, grasslands, mangroves, and other environments across parts of Asia. Unlike lions, tigers are generally solitary animals, patrolling large territories and hunting prey such as deer and wild boar. Despite their strength, they face serious threats from habitat loss, poaching, and conflicts with humans. Fun fact: Every tiger has a unique pattern of stripes, and the markings extend onto its skin beneath the fur. No two tigers have exactly the same stripe pattern.  #Tiger #PantheraTigris #Wildlife #BigCats #Nature
